mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 220i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series 220i engine replacement typically costs between £1,700 and £3,800 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £1,100, reconditioned units from £1,700, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,400. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 2 Series 220i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which typically lasts 2-5 seconds before disappearing as oil pressure builds. This affects both N20-powered (2014-2016) and B48-powered (2016+) 220i models. Other symptoms include a metallic ticking sound, engine hesitation, and in severe cases, the engine management light illuminating with camshaft position errors (P000A, P0016, P0017).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 220i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For an N20-powered 220i (2014-2016) worth £5,000-£8,000, a reconditioned engine at £1,700-£2,400 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For B48 models (2016+) worth £8,000-£15,000, replacement is almost always justified. For G42 models (2021+) worth £15,000+, replacement is a no-brainer. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 220i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 220i engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 220i and the 218i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 220i is powered by a 2.0-litre four-cylinder B48 engine producing 184-192hp, while the 218i uses a 1.5-litre three-cylinder B38 engine producing 136-140hp. The 220i offers significantly more power and torque, making it the sportier choice, but the 218i is more fuel-efficient and lighter.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series 220i engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For petrol 220i models with OPF (Otto Particulate Filter), compliance is confirmed before dispatch.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series 220i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series 220i arrived in 2014 as the mid-range petrol variant across the 2 Series range. Early models (2014-2016) used the N20 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo engine, which was replaced by the more robust B48 family from 2016 onwards across all body styles.

milestones.description: N20B20U0, 2.0L turbo petrol, 184hp (F22 Coupe, F23 Convertible launch)
B48A20A, 2.0L turbo petrol, 192hp (F45 Active Tourer launch, transverse mounting)
B48B20A, 2.0L turbo petrol, 184hp (F22/F23 LCI, N20 replaced)
B48B20M0, 2.0L turbo petrol, 184hp (F22/F23 LCI, OPF-equipped models)
B48B20A, 2.0L turbo petrol, 184hp (G42 220i Coupe, new generation)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 2 Series 220i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 220i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3 (intro, 2-3 sentences): The BMW 2 Series 220i has been powered by two generations of 2.0-litre turbo petrol engines: the earlier N20 (2014-2016) and the later B48 (2016-present). The N20 is notorious for timing chain guide failure, while the B48 suffers primarily from timing chain tensioner wear and VANOS solenoid issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 2 Series 220i N20 Engine Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N20 timing chain guides are made of plastic that can degrade under heat stress. When the guides fail, the chain can stretch or snap, leading to piston-to-valve contact and catastrophic engine damage. This is particularly prevalent in pre-2015 models.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early (rattling noise only)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if engine has suffered internal damage

problems.recommendation: If you own an N20-powered 220i and hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately - preventative replacement is significantly cheaper than a full rebuild after failure. If the chain has already snapped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N20B20U0 BMW 2 Series 220i engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - BMW 2 Series 220i B48 Engine Rattle
problems.rootCause: The B48 uses a single-row timing chain system that has proven prone to premature stretch and guide wear. Unlike older multi-row chains, this design relies on a plastic tensioner rail that degrades faster under heat stress - especially in stop-start urban driving.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner, VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattle is persistent or mileage >70k

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £2,500-£3,600 (matches Section 4's rebuilt figure for B48 codes)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if chain has skipped teeth or caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - for a typical £8,000-£15,000 B48 220i, timing chain replacement is a worthwhile repair. Full engine replacement is justified if internal damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: The B48 timing chain issue is well-documented in BMW Service Bulletin SI B11 01 18. If you hear a metallic rattle on cold start lasting 2-5 seconds, have the car inspected immediately. A full timing chain kit replacement with upgraded components is the most cost-effective long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for B48 BMW 2 Series 220i engine replacement

problems.h4: VANOS Solenoid Failure - BMW 2 Series 220i Rough Idle and Limp Mode
problems.affectedModels: BMW 2 Series 220i (N20 and B48 variants, all years)
problems.rootCause: VANOS solenoids can become clogged with oil sludge, particularly from urban driving and extended oil change intervals. This leads to rough idle, hesitation, and in severe cases, limp mode activation.

repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if cleaning fails or mileage >70k
If VANOS issues persist after replacement

problems.vehicleValueCheck: VANOS repair is a minor expense relative to vehicle value on all 220i variants. Full engine replacement is never needed for VANOS failure alone.
problems.recommendation: VANOS solenoid issues are common on higher-mileage 220i petrol engines. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) can prevent sludge accumulation. If you experience rough idle or hesitation, have the solenoids inspected promptly.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW 2 Series 220i VANOS repair costs
